problem: Build a faster, data-efficient language-conditioned robot policy without large-scale robot-action pretraining.
contribution: TinyVLA adapts compact pretrained VLMs with LoRA and a diffusion-policy decoder, studying model scale and visual/language generalization.
algorithm: Freeze most pretrained transformer weights, train low-rank attention adapters and diffusion action prediction, then merge LoRA weights for inference. This is a generative policy architecture, not an MLP replacement for ACT.
observations: Two RGB views, language instructions and recorded robot state; experiments explicitly modify OpenVLA to accept both views and add FiLM language conditioning to its diffusion baseline.
actions: Seven continuous position/rotation/gripper entries; gripper width0closed/1open. Bimanual tasks require a separate appropriate action contract.
embodiment_and_data: Five single-arm tasks with100demonstrations each; Franka and bimanual UR5 studies. Variants422M,740M and1.3B total parameters have differing trainable subsets; web VLM pretraining is distinct from absent robot pretraining.
experiments: Multitask quality, instruction/background/view/lighting shifts, model-size failures and policy-head ablations. Each view change gets only2trials; bimanual TableIII caption specifies10trials, without a clearly extracted uncertainty/seed convention here.
baselines: Diffusion Policy, Multimodal Diffusion, modified multiview OpenVLA; ACT/MLP heads inside TinyVLA are local architectural ablations, not definitive comparisons against all standalone ACT implementations.

quantitative_result.value: TinyVLA-H single-arm average94.0%; bimanual PlaceTennisBag30±1 versus Diffusion Policy43±2.3, retaining a negative task result. A6000 reported latency14ms versus modified OpenVLA-1B140ms; timing is source-GPU specific.

limitations: Small per-condition generalization samples, source-specific tooling/views and ambiguous printed uncertainty units limit broad interpretation. A strong single-arm average does not establish uniform bimanual advantage or new-robot transfer.
code_and_license: Fulltext methods/results examined; executable source, checkpoint rights and upstream VLM licenses not audited. No local TinyVLA run is claimed.
hardware_adaptation: Compare compact genuine ACT/diffusion baselines before a larger VLM. Require measured camera/state/action mapping and NX profiling; source A6000 latency does not qualify edge execution.

evidence_locations.supports: 100demos, action semantics and negative task result
